23	## Runtime sources and images
24	
25	[`runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json`](../../runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json) is the
26	source of truth for exact dependency commits and the immutable binary base.
27	Builds fetch those commits without patches or moving branch tips. MILES uses the
28	organized adapter hooks; OLMo-core provides the model, objective and checkpoint
29	APIs required by this adapter; olmo-sglang supplies compatible serving models.
30	The ordinary Open Instruct environment keeps its own dependency versions.
31	
32	The MILES pin includes the v0.1.2 async-consumer compatibility fix from
33	[miles-olmo-core PR #10](https://github.com/allenai/miles-olmo-core/pull/10).
34	Its refresh and engine-drain dequeues accept the native consumer's optional trainer
35	identity and preserve Core's explicit rejection of multi-policy training.
36	
37	The binary base contains the compiled dependencies, including FA2, FA3 and FA4.
38	It excludes the MILES, Core, SGLang and Open Instruct source overlays. Application
39	builds add locked source repositories as `runtime-base`, then the committed Open
40	Instruct checkout as `application`. They do not compile FlashAttention, even
41	without a local Docker cache. Source-only lock changes rebuild source layers;
42	binary dependency changes require a new base. Editable installs still fetch
43	build-system dependencies such as setuptools and pybind11, and Megatron builds
44	a small C++ dataset helper. Those build-tool requirements are not fully pinned;
45	the source and base pins do not make application builds bit-for-bit reproducible.
46	
47	The selected base is Beaker `01M5ZYQZVF7DDJ1VR619KRSS42`
48	(`robertb/miles-binary-base-20261027`), Docker
49	`sha256:947e615f93cb88f8739ba270f30adc7f012af8bc0abf43e96f11cd5d3b2d6354`.
50	Its package versions, CPU imports and source isolation were checked, and a pull
51	by immutable ID reproduced the same Docker ID. The
52	[single-GPU Core RL smoke](https://beaker.org/ex/01M61Z3VBAD5219PHZX63YGDY7)
53	passed on application image `01M61Z2XBQB6EP3SJNAX1YN0HV`: four optimizer updates,
54	shared-engine evaluations, checkpoints and HF export on Holmes. This tiny-model
55	check uses Torch attention; it does not qualify every FlashAttention backend or
56	a Qwen OPD GPU training run with the public Megatron sources.
57	The application image (`robertb/miles-main-smoke-5a7be0398`) was built from
58	`5a7be0398e8244cd5376983427e57d4deeea2e39`, Docker
59	`sha256:83cc907a035f98ba69d3b8b7eaaaaa7477d1c06c6efca39da4414ef174df3c67`,
60	and includes the current public source lock and review cleanup.
61	
62	A CPU-only `runtime-base` rebuild from commit
63	`3563eb52ac4b02d731786e8f1a4e39a52951f2a2` is published as Beaker image
64	`01M61YFEWE1BATA8KQ4VAV2DY8` (`robertb/miles-runtime-base-3563eb52a`), Docker
65	`sha256:f97469549508d2af9896161889cc45060c52ece5743ecfcbe937039d3043b784`.
66	Its packaged lock matches the current lock, all six source checkouts match their
67	pinned revisions without patches, and serving/attention CPU imports passed.
68	This records CPU build verification of the runtime sources separately from the
69	application-image GPU smoke above, which subsequently verified the same source lock.
70	
71	The source layer includes Megatron-LM from the Radix fork, pinned to
72	`235952df607b3820716e5e67728a5ab470ca33ae` (the previous runtime's revision,
73	including its Qwen3.5 FP32 optimizer fix), rather than the current `miles-main`
74	tip used by the pinned MILES Dockerfile. Megatron Bridge uses the public Radix
75	revision selected by that Dockerfile. These dependencies support Qwen OPD.
76	The image does not install `olmo-megatron`, the private Olmo Bridge fork, or
77	Olmo-specific Megatron patches; Olmo training uses the Core backend. Package
78	metadata and entrypoints are installed with `--no-deps` to preserve the binary
79	stack. `/src/Megatron-LM` remains a compatibility symlink for the OPD launcher.
80	
81	EOPD metadata transport is implemented in the pinned MILES source, without a
82	local runtime patch. Open Instruct's `opd_hooks` stores teacher top-k values in
83	`Sample.train_metadata`;
84	[rollout conversion](https://github.com/allenai/miles-olmo-core/blob/296a1e80c9c726bc41a764ce7cfcab2c886da64a/miles/ray/rollout/train_data_conversion.py#L173-L174)
85	copies those dictionaries into `train_data["metadata"]`, and the
86	[Megatron training step](https://github.com/allenai/miles-olmo-core/blob/296a1e80c9c726bc41a764ce7cfcab2c886da64a/miles/backends/megatron_utils/model.py#L465-L496)
87	requests `metadata` from `get_batch` for the custom loss. This training field is
88	separate from the input dataset metadata selected by `--metadata-key`.
89	
90	For ordinary application builds:
91	
92	```bash
93	python scripts/miles/build_image.py --base-image LOCAL_LOADED_BASE_IMAGE --tag open-instruct:miles-core
94	```
95	
96	Use `--target runtime-base` to build only the locked dependency sources, without
97	adding the Open Instruct application checkout. The default target is `application`.
98	The image arguments are local Docker tags loaded on the build host; Beaker names
99	and immutable IDs identify the images to pull before invoking the helper.
100	
101	All repositories in the runtime lock are public; no GitHub credential is needed
102	for these source fetches. Standalone source preparation can use
103	`--cache olmo-sglang=/path/to/clone`.
104	Existing published images retain their original sources; rebuild after changing
105	the lock.
106	
107	prepare_runtime refuses to replace existing source directories. Its --cache
108	arguments can use local clones as fetch sources; they do not select uncommitted
109	sibling code. build_image checks the immutable base Docker ID. For actual
110	submission use the [committed-image launcher](launching.md), not a one-off Beaker
111	command with different mounts or source provenance.
112	
113	## Rebuilding the binary base
114	
115	The reproducible maintainer recipe is `runtime/miles/Dockerfile.base`; its two
116	immutable inputs are recorded in `runtime/miles/base-build.lock.json`. Pull both
117	Beaker images into Docker, then run:
118	
119	```bash
120	python scripts/miles/build_base_image.py \
121	  --compiled-parent LOCAL_COMPILED_PARENT \
122	  --flash-attention-builder LOCAL_FA3_BUILDER \
123	  --tag open-instruct:miles-binary-base
124	```
125	
126	Both Docker IDs are verified, and the parent-image label comes from the same
127	lock. The helper passes the compiler image as `FLASH_ATTENTION_BUILDER` and the
128	runtime parent as `COMPILED_PARENT`. Only FA wheels are transferred from the compiler
129	image to the clean compiled parent. FA2/FA4 wheel downloads are checksum-verified;
130	the final stage resets inherited application metadata and entrypoints. This
131	preserves the qualified CUDA/PyTorch stack rather than rebuilding all dependencies
132	from an upstream CUDA distribution. Build on an amd64 Linux host: FA3 compilation
133	defaults to two jobs, with `--max-jobs` available for hosts with sufficient RAM.
134	The published base's FA3 build took about 31 minutes with eight jobs.
135	
136	The final environment list was compared with the locked compiled parent. It
137	preserves its runtime settings while dropping legacy `OLMO_MILES_*` cache and
138	verifier paths. Recheck this list against the parent image whenever changing the
139	parent pin; `FROM scratch` does not inherit environment variables automatically.
140	
141	Before changing the pin again, verify CPU imports, an application build and GPU
142	forward/backward and training on the intended hardware. CPU imports alone do not
143	establish GPU correctness.
144	
145	## Startup dependencies
146	
147	Managed GRPO starts judge loading, Ray startup, and workflow model/data preparation
148	concurrently after assigning GPUs and discovering judge endpoint addresses. Ray
149	readiness and judge known-answer canaries run in separate supervised subprocesses.
150	The driver waits for the exact Ray layout before placement; it waits for judge
151	qualification before generation or evaluation. Readiness files live in the fresh
152	attempt directory, with peer-failure propagation. After replica rendezvous, rank
153	zero writes one `startup.json` deadline shared by all supervisors, readiness
154	probes, and driver barriers. Inventory and service launch consume that same
155	budget; starting a later stage does not reset it. Post-training completion has
156	its own timeout.
157	
158	On disaggregated runs with an explicit rollout count and resident inference,
159	trainer initialization/cache restoration overlaps inference initialization.
160	Connecting trainer parallelism metadata and restoring the rollout cursor remains
161	a barrier after both branches finish, before initial weight publication. Colocated,
162	offloaded-inference, and epoch-derived schedules retain sequential initialization.
163	OPD uses its separate launcher and does not pass through this GRPO supervisor.
164	
165	A failed or cancelled initialization joins its sibling tasks before driver cleanup;
166	the worker manager owns partially initialized remote workers. Cluster supervision
167	also terminates outstanding readiness subprocesses. Judge liveness monitoring
168	starts only after its HTTP endpoint becomes ready.
169	
170	For measurement, the attempt directory contains process start receipts, readiness
171	timestamps. Each probe writes its own timeline under `ray-readiness/driver_timing.jsonl`
172	or `judge-readiness/driver_timing.jsonl`, avoiding concurrent appends on WEKA. The run
173	root has preparation-stage timings; the checkpoint directory has runtime parsing,
174	module import, readiness waits, serving/trainer initialization, connection and
175	publication timings. Overlapping stage durations must not be added together as
176	elapsed startup time. Small-model integration validates ordering and cleanup;
177	full-model wall-time savings require measurement on the intended hardware.
178	
179	## Local development
180	
181	The ordinary CPU suite covers configuration, planning, launch specifications,
182	rewards, data preparation, rendezvous, heartbeat, recovery and topology contracts
183	without installing MILES or
184	SGLang. The `MILES contracts` workflow also checks the maintained scripts and
185	checks application types without requiring the private runtime.
186	Recording and summary implementation tests live with their MILES implementation;
187	Open Instruct keeps record configuration tests and runtime selection/buffer integration tests.
188	The moved adapter is checked against that Core API in the dedicated runtime
189	environment; Open Instruct's ordinary type check covers the application integration.
190	The MoE numerical tests deliberately require the Core revision in the runtime
191	lock. The ordinary `uv.lock` Core version is for existing SFT/DPO paths and is
192	not upgraded to make those runtime-only tests importable.
193	
194	```bash
195	uv run pytest open_instruct/test_miles*.py
196	```
197	
198	The dedicated runtime suite uses the separate application image. From its
199	`/opt/core-rl` working directory, run:
200	
201	```bash
202	bash scripts/miles/test_runtime.sh -q
203	```
204	
205	This command fails if runtime dependencies are missing. Without the explicit
206	runtime flag, ordinary CPU collection omits `tests/miles/` when MILES or SGLang
207	is absent. CUDA numerical cases skip when no GPU is visible. A passing CPU run
208	therefore does not check GPU kernels, distributed gradients or publication.
209	The ordinary Open Instruct GPU CI image does not include the private MILES
210	runtime; dedicated runtime checks are a separate maintainer validation step.
211	
212	For a training lifecycle check, copy [dev.toml](../../configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml)
213	to `runs/`, select a compatible tiny checkpoint, and follow the
214	[committed-image launcher](launching.md). Verify the rendered replica group and
215	retain image, config and completion artifacts. Test refresh separately when
216	changing publication behavior; a tiny mechanics check does not establish learning
217	quality.
218	
219	## Documentation checks
220	
221	```bash
222	python -m scripts.miles.generate_docs --check
223	uv run pytest open_instruct/test_miles_documentation.py
224	uv run mkdocs build
225	make style-check
226	make quality-check
227	```
228	
229	MkDocs generates the four reference pages in memory from configuration sources,
230	the compact pinned parser schema and reviewed `reference-help.json` descriptions.
231	Neither the pages nor native help are tracked. Ordinary documentation builds and
232	local `plan`/`validate` commands need no MILES installation. Without a native help
233	capture, option tables show names, types, choices, restrictions and reviewed
234	supplements; other help and value defaults are explicitly marked unavailable.
235	
236	When runtime pins change, regenerate the compact schema inside the matching
237	runtime and review its diff:
238	
239	```bash
240	python -m scripts.miles.snapshot_options open_instruct/miles/configuration/options.json
241	```
242	
243	For full upstream help and parser defaults, capture an artifact in the pinned
244	runtime using a writable checkout, then supply it to the documentation build:
245	
246	```bash
247	python -m scripts.miles.capture_option_help --image IMMUTABLE_IMAGE_ID --output runs/native-help.json
248	MILES_NATIVE_HELP=runs/native-help.json uv run mkdocs build
249	```
250	
251	The capture checks the installed parser against the expanded compact schema;
252	the docs build rejects stale hashes or missing actions. Parser defaults are not
253	model-dependent resolved defaults. To inspect Markdown separately, run
254	`python -m scripts.miles.generate_docs --output-dir runs/miles-docs` (optionally
255	with `--native-help runs/native-help.json`). `--check` validates the reference
256	inputs without writing files. Edit source definitions and reviewed descriptions,
257	not generated output. Change maintained examples only as a deliberate recipe
258	change; see [development defaults](development-defaults.md).
259	
260	### Type checking the moved adapter
261	
262	In a development environment with the pinned MILES and Core sources, run:
263	
264	```bash
265	ty check /path/to/miles/miles/backends/core_utils --extra-search-path /path/to/OLMo-core/src
266	```
267	
268	Open Instruct's CPU checks do not fetch the private MILES repository. The committed
269	application image and runtime tests check both repositories together.
270	
271	## Adapter package layout
272	
273	`open_instruct/miles/` groups code by responsibility. The public CLI remains
274	`python -m open_instruct.miles`; package initializers do not load the GPU runtime.
275	
276	| Package | Responsibility |
277	|---|---|
278	| `configuration` | RunSpec/CoreConfig, native options, validation, topology and capacity planning |
279	| `execution` | Preparation, Beaker submission, cluster bootstrap and training coordination |
280	| MILES `backends/core_utils` | Core actor, model backends, packing, optimizer scheduling, checkpoints and trainer diagnostics |
281	| `rollout` | Application data-source selection and rollout metrics; managed generation, admission and completed queues live in MILES `backends/core_utils/rollout` |
282	| MILES `backends/core_utils/publication` | Weight delivery, engine drain, policy versions and durable policy state |
283	| `rewards` | Verifiers, reward routing and managed judges |
284	| `datasets` | Dataset preparation, mixtures, inference records and prompt selection |
285	| `evaluation` | Background evaluation submission, workers and result publication |
286	| `infrastructure` | Application artifact publication and bounded infrastructure waits; compiler/HF cache lifecycle lives in MILES |
287	
288	Keep diagnostics next to the component they observe. Keep configuration imports
289	CPU-only, model backends loaded on demand, and package initializers minimal.
290	MILES `backends/core_utils/data.py` adapts samples to the trainer; `rollout/data_source.py` owns
291	runtime data-source behavior; `datasets/run_data.py` prepares researcher inputs.
292	
293	Python integration imports use these package paths, for example
294	`from open_instruct.miles.configuration.run_spec import RunSpec`. The pinned
295	AllenAI MILES fork must use the matching trainer and rollout hook paths. Rebuild
296	the application image when updating this layout and its runtime pin together;
297	existing images retain their original code. Custom verifier factories and saved
298	native options must reference these package paths.
299	
300	The CPU CLI checks in `open_instruct/test_miles_package_layout.py` run without
301	site-packages. `tests/miles/test_package_layout.py` resolves hooks supplied by
302	both repositories inside the pinned runtime.
303	
304	### Application callbacks and CPU tools
305	
306	The backend trainer and managed rollout modules do not import Open Instruct.
307	Open Instruct supplies `core_records_factory` for per-question recording and
308	`core_evaluation_snapshot` for requested post-update HF exports. Those callbacks
309	preserve the existing recording and evaluation schedules. Dataset preparation,
310	reward callbacks, data-source selection, Beaker launch and evaluation submission
311	remain application-owned. The native `olmo_core` argument loader still resolves
312	Open Instruct's run configuration; that is an explicit configuration integration.
313	
314	Small CPU planning and artifact-reader helpers remain local so `plan`, `validate`
315	and offline analysis work without the private runtime. Runtime integration tests
316	compare their algorithms with the MILES counterparts: scoring policy, capacity
317	reporting, timeout diagnostics, atomic JSON publication, input validation and
318	throughput arithmetic.
319	
320	## Core runtime compatibility
321	
322	The `olmo-core` revision in
323	[`runtime.lock.json`](../../runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json) is the Core source used
324	by the runtime. The adapter interfaces it relies on were merged in
325	[OLMo-core PR #888](https://github.com/allenai/OLMo-core/pull/888). The runtime pins
326	merge commit `6ceda6530625caa5d23e3be8a455c600f62a7338`, including the reviewed
327	RoPE import fixes, alongside the MILES v0.1.2 integration.
328	
329	Core's routed-expert `match_eager_rounding` defaults to false. The pinned MILES
330	adapter explicitly enables it for policy scoring and accepts legacy MILES
331	checkpoint manifests with equivalent scoring semantics. Other Core users keep
332	the default behavior.
333	
334	Core's PR checks and application validation cover different boundaries.
335	Rebuild runtime/application images from the lock and validate the intended
336	training topology; an existing image retains its original source revisions.
337	Record application validation with the exact image and source pins. The compact
338	options snapshot must be regenerated whenever runtime source pins change.
339

copies those dictionaries into `train_data["metadata"]`, and the
[Megatron training step](https://github.com/allenai/miles-olmo-core/blob/296a1e80c9c726bc41a764ce7cfcab2c886da64a/miles/backends/megatron_utils/model.py#L465-L496)
requests `metadata` from `get_batch` for the custom loss. This training field is
separate from the input dataset metadata selected by `--metadata-key`.

For ordinary application builds:

```bash
python scripts/miles/build_image.py --base-image LOCAL_LOADED_BASE_IMAGE --tag open-instruct:miles-core
```

Use `--target runtime-base` to build only the locked dependency sources, without
adding the Open Instruct application checkout. The default target is `application`.
The image arguments are local Docker tags loaded on the build host; Beaker names
and immutable IDs identify the images to pull before invoking the helper.

All repositories in the runtime lock are public; no GitHub credential is needed
for these source fetches. Standalone source preparation can use
`--cache olmo-sglang=/path/to/clone`.
Existing published images retain their original sources; rebuild after changing
the lock.

prepare_runtime refuses to replace existing source directories. Its --cache
arguments can use local clones as fetch sources; they do not select uncommitted
sibling code. build_image checks the immutable base Docker ID. For actual
submission use the [committed-image launcher](launching.md), not a one-off Beaker
command with different mounts or source provenance.

## Rebuilding the binary base

The reproducible maintainer recipe is `runtime/miles/Dockerfile.base`; its two
immutable inputs are recorded in `runtime/miles/base-build.lock.json`. Pull both
Beaker images into Docker, then run:

```bash
python scripts/miles/build_base_image.py \
  --compiled-parent LOCAL_COMPILED_PARENT \
  --flash-attention-builder LOCAL_FA3_BUILDER \
  --tag open-instruct:miles-binary-base
```

Both Docker IDs are verified, and the parent-image label comes from the same
lock. The helper passes the compiler image as `FLASH_ATTENTION_BUILDER` and the
runtime parent as `COMPILED_PARENT`. Only FA wheels are transferred from the compiler
image to the clean compiled parent. FA2/FA4 wheel downloads are checksum-verified;
the final stage resets inherited application metadata and entrypoints. This
preserves the qualified CUDA/PyTorch stack rather than rebuilding all dependencies
from an upstream CUDA distribution. Build on an amd64 Linux host: FA3 compilation
defaults to two jobs, with `--max-jobs` available for hosts with sufficient RAM.
The published base's FA3 build took about 31 minutes with eight jobs.

The final environment list was compared with the locked compiled parent. It
preserves its runtime settings while dropping legacy `OLMO_MILES_*` cache and
verifier paths. Recheck this list against the parent image whenever changing the
parent pin; `FROM scratch` does not inherit environment variables automatically.

Before changing the pin again, verify CPU imports, an application build and GPU
forward/backward and training on the intended hardware. CPU imports alone do not
establish GPU correctness.

## Startup dependencies

Managed GRPO starts judge loading, Ray startup, and workflow model/data preparation
concurrently after assigning GPUs and discovering judge endpoint addresses. Ray
readiness and judge known-answer canaries run in separate supervised subprocesses.
The driver waits for the exact Ray layout before placement; it waits for judge
qualification before generation or evaluation. Readiness files live in the fresh
attempt directory, with peer-failure propagation. After replica rendezvous, rank
zero writes one `startup.json` deadline shared by all supervisors, readiness
probes, and driver barriers. Inventory and service launch consume that same
budget; starting a later stage does not reset it. Post-training completion has
its own timeout.

On disaggregated runs with an explicit rollout count and resident inference,
trainer initialization/cache restoration overlaps inference initialization.
Connecting trainer parallelism metadata and restoring the rollout cursor remains
a barrier after both branches finish, before initial weight publication. Colocated,
offloaded-inference, and epoch-derived schedules retain sequential initialization.
OPD uses its separate launcher and does not pass through this GRPO supervisor.

A failed or cancelled initialization joins its sibling tasks before driver cleanup;
the worker manager owns partially initialized remote workers. Cluster supervision
also terminates outstanding readiness subprocesses. Judge liveness monitoring
starts only after its HTTP endpoint becomes ready.

For measurement, the attempt directory contains process start receipts, readiness
timestamps. Each probe writes its own timeline under `ray-readiness/driver_timing.jsonl`
or `judge-readiness/driver_timing.jsonl`, avoiding concurrent appends on WEKA. The run
root has preparation-stage timings; the checkpoint directory has runtime parsing,
module import, readiness waits, serving/trainer initialization, connection and
publication timings. Overlapping stage durations must not be added together as
elapsed startup time. Small-model integration validates ordering and cleanup;
full-model wall-time savings require measurement on the intended hardware.

## Local development

The ordinary CPU suite covers configuration, planning, launch specifications,
rewards, data preparation, rendezvous, heartbeat, recovery and topology contracts
without installing MILES or
SGLang. The `MILES contracts` workflow also checks the maintained scripts and
checks application types without requiring the private runtime.
Recording and summary implementation tests live with their MILES implementation;
Open Instruct keeps record configuration tests and runtime selection/buffer integration tests.
The moved adapter is checked against that Core API in the dedicated runtime
environment; Open Instruct's ordinary type check covers the application integration.
The MoE numerical tests deliberately require the Core revision in the runtime
lock. The ordinary `uv.lock` Core version is for existing SFT/DPO paths and is
not upgraded to make those runtime-only tests importable.

```bash
uv run pytest open_instruct/test_miles*.py
```

The dedicated runtime suite uses the separate application image. From its
`/opt/core-rl` working directory, run:

```bash
bash scripts/miles/test_runtime.sh -q
```

This command fails if runtime dependencies are missing. Without the explicit
runtime flag, ordinary CPU collection omits `tests/miles/` when MILES or SGLang
is absent. CUDA numerical cases skip when no GPU is visible. A passing CPU run
therefore does not check GPU kernels, distributed gradients or publication.
The ordinary Open Instruct GPU CI image does not include the private MILES
runtime; dedicated runtime checks are a separate maintainer validation step.

For a training lifecycle check, copy [dev.toml](../../configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml)
to `runs/`, select a compatible tiny checkpoint, and follow the
[committed-image launcher](launching.md). Verify the rendered replica group and
retain image, config and completion artifacts. Test refresh separately when
changing publication behavior; a tiny mechanics check does not establish learning
quality.

## Documentation checks

```bash
python -m scripts.miles.generate_docs --check
uv run pytest open_instruct/test_miles_documentation.py
uv run mkdocs build
make style-check
make quality-check
```

MkDocs generates the four reference pages in memory from configuration sources,
the compact pinned parser schema and reviewed `reference-help.json` descriptions.
Neither the pages nor native help are tracked. Ordinary documentation builds and
local `plan`/`validate` commands need no MILES installation. Without a native help
capture, option tables show names, types, choices, restrictions and reviewed
supplements; other help and value defaults are explicitly marked unavailable.

When runtime pins change, regenerate the compact schema inside the matching
runtime and review its diff:

```bash
python -m scripts.miles.snapshot_options open_instruct/miles/configuration/options.json
```

For full upstream help and parser defaults, capture an artifact in the pinned
runtime using a writable checkout, then supply it to the documentation build:

```bash
python -m scripts.miles.capture_option_help --image IMMUTABLE_IMAGE_ID --output runs/native-help.json
MILES_NATIVE_HELP=runs/native-help.json uv run mkdocs build
```

The capture checks the installed parser against the expanded compact schema;
the docs build rejects stale hashes or missing actions. Parser defaults are not
model-dependent resolved defaults. To inspect Markdown separately, run
`python -m scripts.miles.generate_docs --output-dir runs/miles-docs` (optionally
with `--native-help runs/native-help.json`). `--check` validates the reference
inputs without writing files. Edit source definitions and reviewed descriptions,
not generated output. Change maintained examples only as a deliberate recipe
change; see [development defaults](development-defaults.md).

### Type checking the moved adapter

In a development environment with the pinned MILES and Core sources, run:

```bash
ty check /path/to/miles/miles/backends/core_utils --extra-search-path /path/to/OLMo-core/src
```

Open Instruct's CPU checks do not fetch the private MILES repository. The committed
application image and runtime tests check both repositories together.

## Adapter package layout

`open_instruct/miles/` groups code by responsibility. The public CLI remains
`python -m open_instruct.miles`; package initializers do not load the GPU runtime.

| Package | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `configuration` | RunSpec/CoreConfig, native options, validation, topology and capacity planning |
| `execution` | Preparation, Beaker submission, cluster bootstrap and training coordination |
| MILES `backends/core_utils` | Core actor, model backends, packing, optimizer scheduling, checkpoints and trainer diagnostics |
| `rollout` | Application data-source selection and rollout metrics; managed generation, admission and completed queues live in MILES `backends/core_utils/rollout` |
| MILES `backends/core_utils/publication` | Weight delivery, engine drain, policy versions and durable policy state |
| `rewards` | Verifiers, reward routing and managed judges |
| `datasets` | Dataset preparation, mixtures, inference records and prompt selection |
| `evaluation` | Background evaluation submission, workers and result publication |
| `infrastructure` | Application artifact publication and bounded infrastructure waits; compiler/HF cache lifecycle lives in MILES |

Keep diagnostics next to the component they observe. Keep configuration imports
CPU-only, model backends loaded on demand, and package initializers minimal.
MILES `backends/core_utils/data.py` adapts samples to the trainer; `rollout/data_source.py` owns
runtime data-source behavior; `datasets/run_data.py` prepares researcher inputs.

Python integration imports use these package paths, for example
`from open_instruct.miles.configuration.run_spec import RunSpec`. The pinned
AllenAI MILES fork must use the matching trainer and rollout hook paths. Rebuild
the application image when updating this layout and its runtime pin together;
existing images retain their original code. Custom verifier factories and saved
native options must reference these package paths.

The CPU CLI checks in `open_instruct/test_miles_package_layout.py` run without
site-packages. `tests/miles/test_package_layout.py` resolves hooks supplied by
both repositories inside the pinned runtime.

### Application callbacks and CPU tools

The backend trainer and managed rollout modules do not import Open Instruct.
Open Instruct supplies `core_records_factory` for per-question recording and
`core_evaluation_snapshot` for requested post-update HF exports. Those callbacks
preserve the existing recording and evaluation schedules. Dataset preparation,
reward callbacks, data-source selection, Beaker launch and evaluation submission
remain application-owned. The native `olmo_core` argument loader still resolves
Open Instruct's run configuration; that is an explicit configuration integration.

Small CPU planning and artifact-reader helpers remain local so `plan`, `validate`
and offline analysis work without the private runtime. Runtime integration tests
compare their algorithms with the MILES counterparts: scoring policy, capacity
reporting, timeout diagnostics, atomic JSON publication, input validation and
throughput arithmetic.

## Core runtime compatibility

The `olmo-core` revision in
[`runtime.lock.json`](../../runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json) is the Core source used
by the runtime. The adapter interfaces it relies on were merged in
[OLMo-core PR #888](https://github.com/allenai/OLMo-core/pull/888). The runtime pins
merge commit `6ceda6530625caa5d23e3be8a455c600f62a7338`, including the reviewed
RoPE import fixes, alongside the MILES v0.1.2 integration.

Core's routed-expert `match_eager_rounding` defaults to false. The pinned MILES
adapter explicitly enables it for policy scoring and accepts legacy MILES
checkpoint manifests with equivalent scoring semantics. Other Core users keep
the default behavior.

Core's PR checks and application validation cover different boundaries.
Rebuild runtime/application images from the lock and validate the intended
training topology; an existing image retains its original source revisions.
Record application validation with the exact image and source pins. The compact
options snapshot must be regenerated whenever runtime source pins change.

159	trainer initialization/cache restoration overlaps inference initialization.
160	Connecting trainer parallelism metadata and restoring the rollout cursor remains
161	a barrier after both branches finish, before initial weight publication. Colocated,
162	offloaded-inference, and epoch-derived schedules retain sequential initialization.
163	OPD uses its separate launcher and does not pass through this GRPO supervisor.
164	
165	A failed or cancelled initialization joins its sibling tasks before driver cleanup;
166	the worker manager owns partially initialized remote workers. Cluster supervision
167	also terminates outstanding readiness subprocesses. Judge liveness monitoring
168	starts only after its HTTP endpoint becomes ready.
169	
170	For measurement, the attempt directory contains process start receipts, readiness
171	timestamps. Each probe writes its own timeline under `ray-readiness/driver_timing.jsonl`
172	or `judge-readiness/driver_timing.jsonl`, avoiding concurrent appends on WEKA. The run
173	root has preparation-stage timings; the checkpoint directory has runtime parsing,
174	module import, readiness waits, serving/trainer initialization, connection and
175	publication timings. Overlapping stage durations must not be added together as
176	elapsed startup time. Small-model integration validates ordering and cleanup;
177	full-model wall-time savings require measurement on the intended hardware.
178	
179	## Local development
180	
181	The ordinary CPU suite covers configuration, planning, launch specifications,
182	rewards, data preparation, rendezvous, heartbeat, recovery and topology contracts
183	without installing MILES or
184	SGLang. The `MILES contracts` workflow also checks the maintained scripts and
185	checks application types without requiring the private runtime.
186	Recording and summary implementation tests live with their MILES implementation;
187	Open Instruct keeps record configuration tests and runtime selection/buffer integration tests.
188	The moved adapter is checked against that Core API in the dedicated runtime
189	environment; Open Instruct's ordinary type check covers the application integration.
190	The MoE numerical tests deliberately require the Core revision in the runtime
191	lock. The ordinary `uv.lock` Core version is for existing SFT/DPO paths and is
192	not upgraded to make those runtime-only tests importable.
193	
194	```bash
195	uv run pytest open_instruct/test_miles*.py
196	```
197	
198	The dedicated runtime suite uses the separate application image. From its
199	`/opt/core-rl` working directory, run:
200	
201	```bash
202	bash scripts/miles/test_runtime.sh -q
203	```
204	
205	This command fails if runtime dependencies are missing. Without the explicit
206	runtime flag, ordinary CPU collection omits `tests/miles/` when MILES or SGLang
207	is absent. CUDA numerical cases skip when no GPU is visible. A passing CPU run
208	therefore does not check GPU kernels, distributed gradients or publication.
209	The ordinary Open Instruct GPU CI image does not include the private MILES
210	runtime; dedicated runtime checks are a separate maintainer validation step.
211	
212	For a training lifecycle check, copy [dev.toml](../../configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml)
213	to `runs/`, select a compatible tiny checkpoint, and follow the
214	[committed-image launcher](launching.md). Verify the rendered replica group and
215	retain image, config and completion artifacts. Test refresh separately when
216	changing publication behavior; a tiny mechanics check does not establish learning
217	quality.
218	
219	## Documentation checks
220	
221	```bash
222	python -m scripts.miles.generate_docs --check
223	uv run pytest open_instruct/test_miles_documentation.py
224	uv run mkdocs build
225	make style-check
226	make quality-check
227	```
228	
229	MkDocs generates the four reference pages in memory from configuration sources,
230	the compact pinned parser schema and reviewed `reference-help.json` descriptions.
231	Neither the pages nor native help are tracked. Ordinary documentation builds and
232	local `plan`/`validate` commands need no MILES installation. Without a native help
233	capture, option tables show names, types, choices, restrictions and reviewed
234	supplements; other help and value defaults are explicitly marked unavailable.
235	
236	When runtime pins change, regenerate the compact schema inside the matching
237	runtime and review its diff:
238	
239	```bash
240	python -m scripts.miles.snapshot_options open_instruct/miles/configuration/options.json
241	```
242	
243	For full upstream help and parser defaults, capture an artifact in the pinned
244	runtime using a writable checkout, then supply it to the documentation build:
245	
246	```bash
247	python -m scripts.miles.capture_option_help --image IMMUTABLE_IMAGE_ID --output runs/native-help.json
248	MILES_NATIVE_HELP=runs/native-help.json uv run mkdocs build
249	```
250	
251	The capture checks the installed parser against the expanded compact schema;
252	the docs build rejects stale hashes or missing actions. Parser defaults are not
253	model-dependent resolved defaults. To inspect Markdown separately, run
254	`python -m scripts.miles.generate_docs --output-dir runs/miles-docs` (optionally
255	with `--native-help runs/native-help.json`). `--check` validates the reference
256	inputs without writing files. Edit source definitions and reviewed descriptions,
257	not generated output. Change maintained examples only as a deliberate recipe
258	change; see [development defaults](development-defaults.md).
259	
260	### Type checking the moved adapter
261	
262	In a development environment with the pinned MILES and Core sources, run:
263	
264	```bash
265	ty check /path/to/miles/miles/backends/core_utils --extra-search-path /path/to/OLMo-core/src
266	```
267	
268	Open Instruct's CPU checks do not fetch the private MILES repository. The committed
269	application image and runtime tests check both repositories together.
270	
271	## Adapter package layout
272	
273	`open_instruct/miles/` groups code by responsibility. The public CLI remains
274	`python -m open_instruct.miles`; package initializers do not load the GPU runtime.
275	
276	| Package | Responsibility |
277	|---|---|
278	| `configuration` | RunSpec/CoreConfig, native options, validation, topology and capacity planning |
279	| `execution` | Preparation, Beaker submission, cluster bootstrap and training coordination |
280	| MILES `backends/core_utils` | Core actor, model backends, packing, optimizer scheduling, checkpoints and trainer diagnostics |
281	| `rollout` | Application data-source selection and rollout metrics; managed generation, admission and completed queues live in MILES `backends/core_utils/rollout` |
282	| MILES `backends/core_utils/publication` | Weight delivery, engine drain, policy versions and durable policy state |
283	| `rewards` | Verifiers, reward routing and managed judges |
284	| `datasets` | Dataset preparation, mixtures, inference records and prompt selection |
285	| `evaluation` | Background evaluation submission, workers and result publication |
286	| `infrastructure` | Application artifact publication and bounded infrastructure waits; compiler/HF cache lifecycle lives in MILES |
287	
288	Keep diagnostics next to the component they observe. Keep configuration imports
289	CPU-only, model backends loaded on demand, and package initializers minimal.
290	MILES `backends/core_utils/data.py` adapts samples to the trainer; `rollout/data_source.py` owns
291	runtime data-source behavior; `datasets/run_data.py` prepares researcher inputs.
292	
293	Python integration imports use these package paths, for example
294	`from open_instruct.miles.configuration.run_spec import RunSpec`. The pinned
295	AllenAI MILES fork must use the matching trainer and rollout hook paths. Rebuild
296	the application image when updating this layout and its runtime pin together;
297	existing images retain their original code. Custom verifier factories and saved
298	native options must reference these package paths.
299	
300	The CPU CLI checks in `open_instruct/test_miles_package_layout.py` run without
301	site-packages. `tests/miles/test_package_layout.py` resolves hooks supplied by
302	both repositories inside the pinned runtime.
303	
304	### Application callbacks and CPU tools
305	
306	The backend trainer and managed rollout modules do not import Open Instruct.
307	Open Instruct supplies `core_records_factory` for per-question recording and
308	`core_evaluation_snapshot` for requested post-update HF exports. Those callbacks
309	preserve the existing recording and evaluation schedules. Dataset preparation,
310	reward callbacks, data-source selection, Beaker launch and evaluation submission
311	remain application-owned. The native `olmo_core` argument loader still resolves
312	Open Instruct's run configuration; that is an explicit configuration integration.
313	
314	Small CPU planning and artifact-reader helpers remain local so `plan`, `validate`
315	and offline analysis work without the private runtime. Runtime integration tests
316	compare their algorithms with the MILES counterparts: scoring policy, capacity
317	reporting, timeout diagnostics, atomic JSON publication, input validation and
318	throughput arithmetic.
319	
320	## Core runtime compatibility
321	
322	The `olmo-core` revision in
323	[`runtime.lock.json`](../../runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json) is the Core source used
324	by the runtime. The adapter interfaces it relies on were merged in
325	[OLMo-core PR #888](https://github.com/allenai/OLMo-core/pull/888). The runtime pins
326	merge commit `6ceda6530625caa5d23e3be8a455c600f62a7338`, including the reviewed
327	RoPE import fixes, alongside the MILES v0.1.2 integration.
328	
329	Core's routed-expert `match_eager_rounding` defaults to false. The pinned MILES
330	adapter explicitly enables it for policy scoring and accepts legacy MILES
331	checkpoint manifests with equivalent scoring semantics. Other Core users keep
332	the default behavior.
333	
334	Core's PR checks and application validation cover different boundaries.
335	Rebuild runtime/application images from the lock and validate the intended
336	training topology; an existing image retains its original source revisions.
337	Record application validation with the exact image and source pins. The compact
338	options snapshot must be regenerated whenever runtime source pins change.
339

"""Expose the MILES workflow and inference-record tools through one command-line entry
point. The CLI loads run files and overrides for planning, validation, local
execution, Beaker submission and status queries, or dispatches record analysis and
prompt-selection commands. Runtime imports are deferred to the commands that need
them so planning remains available without the GPU stack.

Run with python -m open_instruct.miles {plan,validate,train,run,status} CONFIG.toml.

Inference-record tools use their own arguments:
python -m open_instruct.miles records summarize STORE --output DIR
python -m open_instruct.miles records select STORE --skip all_zero --output TABLE.json
"""

import argparse
import importlib
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from open_instruct.miles.configuration import advisories, specs, validation
from open_instruct.miles.configuration.config import RunConfig
from open_instruct.miles.distillation import opd_config
from open_instruct.miles.errors import InputError


def main() -> None:
    if sys.argv[1:2] == ["records"]:
        module = (
            "open_instruct.miles.datasets.replay_summary"
            if sys.argv[2:3] == ["replay-pool"]
            else "open_instruct.miles.datasets.record_selection"
            if sys.argv[2:3] == ["select"]
            else "miles.utils.record_summary"
        )
        try:
            command = importlib.import_module(module)
        except ModuleNotFoundError as error:
            if error.name == "miles":
                raise SystemExit(
                    "Record analysis requires the MILES package; run it in the pinned runtime."
                ) from error
            raise
        command.main(sys.argv[3:] if sys.argv[2:3] in (["select"], ["replay-pool"]) else sys.argv[2:])
        return
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("command", choices=("plan", "validate", "train", "run", "status"))
    parser.add_argument("config", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--set",
        dest="overrides",
        action="append",
        default=[],
        metavar="SECTION.KEY=VALUE",
        help="Override a setting with a TOML value; repeatable, quote strings",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--debug", action="store_true", help="Show a full traceback for input errors")
    options = parser.parse_args()
    try:
        execute(parser, options)
    except InputError as error:
        if options.debug:
            raise
        parser.error(f"{options.config}: {error}")


def execute(parser, options):
    payload = validation.read_document(options.config)
    structured = "schema_version" in payload or "model" in payload
    config = (
        specs.from_dict(payload, config_path=options.config, overrides=options.overrides)
        if structured
        else RunConfig.from_dict(payload, options.overrides)
    )
    if options.command == "plan":
        planned = config.plan()
        advisories.emit(planned)
        print(json.dumps(planned, indent=2))
        return
    if options.command in ("run", "status"):
        if not structured:
            parser.error("run/status require a schema_version=1 run file; raw configs support plan/validate/train")
        launch = importlib.import_module("open_instruct.miles.execution.launch")
        if options.command == "run":
            launch.run(options.config, options.overrides)
        else:
            print(json.dumps(launch.status(config), indent=2))
        return
    if isinstance(config, opd_config.OPDRunSpec):
        if options.command == "validate":
            config.plan()
            print("OPD schema and allocation validated; runtime/model checks run in the candidate image")
        else:
            runtime = importlib.import_module("open_instruct.miles.distillation.opd_runtime")
            runtime.execute(config)
        return
    workflow = importlib.import_module("open_instruct.miles.execution.workflow")
    if options.command == "validate":
        if structured:
            planned_spec = config.plan()  # Validate physical allocation as well as trainer options.
            advisories.emit(planned_spec)
            print("Run schema, topology and MILES/Core options validated; inputs and runtime checked during train")
        else:
            workflow.parse_runtime(config)
            print("MILES arguments validated for OLMo-core")
        return
    if structured:
        workflow.execute(config)
    else:
        workflow.train_config(config)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

1	# MILES GRPO
2	
3	MILES GRPO is the recommended path for reinforcement learning with supported
4	Olmo MoE models through Open Instruct, with OLMo-core training and SGLang inference.
5	Existing [Core/vLLM and DeepSpeed/vLLM workflows](../algorithms/grpo.md) remain
6	available for dense-model training. This guide covers setup, the pinned runtime
7	and a first run. See [support and limits](feature-parity.md) for what is available
8	and [development defaults](development-defaults.md) for starting settings.
9	
10	## Run MILES GRPO
11	
12	1. Check [model and topology support](models-and-checkpoints.md), check out the
13	   intended Open Instruct revision, then follow the
14	   [laptop/session setup](launching.md). Sibling development worktrees are unnecessary.
15	2. Copy [dev.toml](../../configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml) to ignored
16	   `runs/my-grpo.toml`. Set a run name, fresh output path and compatible tiny
17	   checkpoint for a single-GPU colocated mechanics check. Keep barrier publication
18	   and offline W&B for this first exercise unless requested otherwise.
19	   Use [node.toml](../../configs/miles/examples/tiny/node.toml)
20	   for single-node math, instruction-following and code training, after preparing
21	   its policy, data and code-verifier service. It allocates no judge GPU.
22	3. Check Beaker resource access and supply credentials for the selected inputs
23	   and tracking mode. Run `plan` and `validate`, then inspect the rendered Beaker
24	   spec against the [distributed scheduling contract](launching.md#distributed-scheduling-contract);
25	   those commands alone do not check that contract. Set `MILES_EXISTING_IMAGE`
26	   to the immutable image ID and invoke
27	   `python -m open_instruct.miles run /path/to/run.toml` through the committed-image
28	   wrapper. Verify replica grouping and placement after submission.
29	4. Retain the launch receipt, submitted TOML and [completion artifacts](operations.md).
30	   Follow the run to completion and report the experiment link, image, model,
31	   configuration and validation outcomes.
32	
33	The submitting host needs Python 3.12 and the Beaker CLI. Training runs use a
34	separate image built from the selected application revision and
35	[`runtime.lock.json`](../../runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json). Building that image
36	currently requires access to private AI2 source repositories and the pinned
37	binary base; this integration is not a self-contained public training install.
38	See [image setup](launching.md#laptop-choose-or-build-an-image).
39	The submission host does not need the local CUDA training stack. Example model
40	and data paths are placeholders that must be replaced for the selected run.
41	
42	## Configuration conventions
43	
44	The maintained examples are `dev.toml`, `node.toml` and `three-node.toml`
45	under `configs/miles/examples/`. Keep these templates unchanged for individual
46	runs. Copy one to Git-ignored `runs/` for experiments, sweeps and debugging.
47	Add a maintained example only for an agreed, distinct user-facing purpose;
48	otherwise update an existing tier. Tests must not depend on untracked run files.
49	Keep historical provenance in measurement reports and immutable run artifacts.
50	
51	For disposable runs without checkpoint/resume testing or saved-weight needs, set
52	`training.save_checkpoints=false` and `output.export_hf=false`, and remove any
53	explicit `save_interval`. Rollout capture defaults off; set
54	`output.rollout_sample_rate` when whole-group captures are needed for analysis
55	(`1` keeps every group).
56	
57	New asynchronous runs start with `async.max_weight_staleness=6`, compiled to
58	`core.max_policy_lag=6`. Set the latter explicitly in low-level `[core]`/`[miles]`
59	configurations. Preserve user overrides and historical reproduction settings;
60	synchronous mechanics runs retain zero lag. Six is a starting point, not an
61	optimum for every workload. See [policy lag and TIS](async-pipeline.md#policy-lag-and-tis)
62	and [development defaults](development-defaults.md).
63	
64	## Router auxiliary losses in the examples
65	
66	The three maintained examples set both router balancing and z-loss coefficients
67	to zero; low-level API defaults remain nonzero. Re-enable either coefficient
68	explicitly to train with auxiliary losses. See
69	[router auxiliary objectives](core.md#router-auxiliary-objectives) for the controls.
70	
71	## Experimental expert-aware packing
72	
73	Replay-informed expert-aware packing is **experimental and disabled by default**
74	in all maintained examples. Opt in with `trainer.expert_balanced_packing=true`
75	only on a supported topology. Planning overhead can offset training savings;
76	measure end-to-end update time before adopting it. See [requirements and
77	controls](sequence-packing.md#replay-informed-expert-aware-packing-experimental).
78	
79	## Online filtering default
80	
81	Learning runs enable `training.filter_zero_std_groups=true`: constant-reward prompt
82	groups are dropped and generation replenishes the accepted training batch. Offline
83	correctness preprocessing can still be applied. The tiny `dev` mechanics
84	example explicitly disables filtering to permit all-zero-reward checks. See
85	[data and evaluation](data-and-evaluation.md#online-group-filtering) for metrics,
86	batch semantics and the opt-out.
87	
88	## Truncated responses
89	
90	The demo configs are the baseline for configuration choices unless a run explicitly
91	states otherwise. GRPO uses **per-response loss weighting** and **zero reward for
92	length-truncated responses**. The Core reward default also scores truncations zero,
93	so omitting the field does not silently change the objective. The examples make
94	these choices explicit:
95	
96	```toml
97	[core]
98	reward_zero_truncated = true
99	
100	[miles]
101	calculate_per_token_loss = false
102	```
103	
104	This works with every verifier, managed judges included. It cannot be combined
105	with a `custom_reward_post_process_path` other than the default ungraded-response
106	exclusion described below. Final-answer selection and explicit verifier exceptions
107	are described in [Grading inputs and changes](grading.md).
108	
109	## Ungraded responses
110	
111	A verifier or judge request can fail for reasons unrelated to the response: a
112	code-service outage, a judge transport error, an unparseable verdict. That
113	response has no grade. Scoring it zero would place a correct answer below its
114	siblings' baseline and push the policy away from it; dropping its prompt group
115	would waste every graded sibling. By default (`core.exclude_ungraded = true`) the
116	compiler installs
117	`custom_reward_post_process_path = "open_instruct.miles.rewards.exclusion.exclude_ungraded"`:
118	the ungraded response gets zero advantage and a zeroed loss mask, its group's
119	baseline uses only the graded responses, and the paired group filter ignores it
120	when checking reward variation (groups with fewer than two graded responses are
121	dropped). The failed response keeps `metadata.reward_omission` with the verifier
122	name and error, and W&B reports `rollout/verification/ungraded_samples` and
123	`ungraded_fraction` per collection. With response-averaged loss, excluded responses
124	still count in the batch denominator, so a high failure fraction reduces the
125	policy-gradient signal per step. Groups with no trainable responses are
126	always rejected, even with `filter_zero_std_groups=false`; that setting keeps
127	valid all-zero grades, not empty groups. The collector requests replacement groups.
128	A run where every group is rejected makes no optimizer progress.
129	
130	Set `core.exclude_ungraded = false` to return to omitting the whole prompt group
131	(`rollout/verification/omitted_records`). The compiler also leaves the hook out
132	under `core.expert_balanced_packing`, which supports no reward post-process, and
133	under `miles.partial_rollout`, since the hook supports single-segment rollouts

# MILES GRPO

MILES GRPO is the recommended path for reinforcement learning with supported
Olmo MoE models through Open Instruct, with OLMo-core training and SGLang inference.
Existing [Core/vLLM and DeepSpeed/vLLM workflows](../algorithms/grpo.md) remain
available for dense-model training. This guide covers setup, the pinned runtime
and a first run. See [support and limits](feature-parity.md) for what is available
and [development defaults](development-defaults.md) for starting settings.

## Run MILES GRPO

1. Check [model and topology support](models-and-checkpoints.md), check out the
   intended Open Instruct revision, then follow the
   [laptop/session setup](launching.md). Sibling development worktrees are unnecessary.
2. Copy [dev.toml](../../configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml) to ignored
   `runs/my-grpo.toml`. Set a run name, fresh output path and compatible tiny
   checkpoint for a single-GPU colocated mechanics check. Keep barrier publication
   and offline W&B for this first exercise unless requested otherwise.
   Use [node.toml](../../configs/miles/examples/tiny/node.toml)
   for single-node math, instruction-following and code training, after preparing
   its policy, data and code-verifier service. It allocates no judge GPU.
3. Check Beaker resource access and supply credentials for the selected inputs
   and tracking mode. Run `plan` and `validate`, then inspect the rendered Beaker
   spec against the [distributed scheduling contract](launching.md#distributed-scheduling-contract);
   those commands alone do not check that contract. Set `MILES_EXISTING_IMAGE`
   to the immutable image ID and invoke
   `python -m open_instruct.miles run /path/to/run.toml` through the committed-image
   wrapper. Verify replica grouping and placement after submission.
4. Retain the launch receipt, submitted TOML and [completion artifacts](operations.md).
   Follow the run to completion and report the experiment link, image, model,
   configuration and validation outcomes.

The submitting host needs Python 3.12 and the Beaker CLI. Training runs use a
separate image built from the selected application revision and
[`runtime.lock.json`](../../runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json). Building that image
currently requires access to private AI2 source repositories and the pinned
binary base; this integration is not a self-contained public training install.
See [image setup](launching.md#laptop-choose-or-build-an-image).
The submission host does not need the local CUDA training stack. Example model
and data paths are placeholders that must be replaced for the selected run.

## Configuration conventions

The maintained examples are `dev.toml`, `node.toml` and `three-node.toml`
under `configs/miles/examples/`. Keep these templates unchanged for individual
runs. Copy one to Git-ignored `runs/` for experiments, sweeps and debugging.
Add a maintained example only for an agreed, distinct user-facing purpose;
otherwise update an existing tier. Tests must not depend on untracked run files.
Keep historical provenance in measurement reports and immutable run artifacts.

For disposable runs without checkpoint/resume testing or saved-weight needs, set
`training.save_checkpoints=false` and `output.export_hf=false`, and remove any
explicit `save_interval`. Rollout capture defaults off; set
`output.rollout_sample_rate` when whole-group captures are needed for analysis
(`1` keeps every group).

New asynchronous runs start with `async.max_weight_staleness=6`, compiled to
`core.max_policy_lag=6`. Set the latter explicitly in low-level `[core]`/`[miles]`
configurations. Preserve user overrides and historical reproduction settings;
synchronous mechanics runs retain zero lag. Six is a starting point, not an
optimum for every workload. See [policy lag and TIS](async-pipeline.md#policy-lag-and-tis)
and [development defaults](development-defaults.md).

## Router auxiliary losses in the examples

The three maintained examples set both router balancing and z-loss coefficients
to zero; low-level API defaults remain nonzero. Re-enable either coefficient
explicitly to train with auxiliary losses. See
[router auxiliary objectives](core.md#router-auxiliary-objectives) for the controls.

## Experimental expert-aware packing

Replay-informed expert-aware packing is **experimental and disabled by default**
in all maintained examples. Opt in with `trainer.expert_balanced_packing=true`
only on a supported topology. Planning overhead can offset training savings;
measure end-to-end update time before adopting it. See [requirements and
controls](sequence-packing.md#replay-informed-expert-aware-packing-experimental).

## Online filtering default

Learning runs enable `training.filter_zero_std_groups=true`: constant-reward prompt
groups are dropped and generation replenishes the accepted training batch. Offline
correctness preprocessing can still be applied. The tiny `dev` mechanics
example explicitly disables filtering to permit all-zero-reward checks. See
[data and evaluation](data-and-evaluation.md#online-group-filtering) for metrics,
batch semantics and the opt-out.

## Truncated responses

The demo configs are the baseline for configuration choices unless a run explicitly
states otherwise. GRPO uses **per-response loss weighting** and **zero reward for
length-truncated responses**. The Core reward default also scores truncations zero,
so omitting the field does not silently change the objective. The examples make
these choices explicit:

```toml
[core]
reward_zero_truncated = true

[miles]
calculate_per_token_loss = false
```

This works with every verifier, managed judges included. It cannot be combined
with a `custom_reward_post_process_path` other than the default ungraded-response
exclusion described below. Final-answer selection and explicit verifier exceptions
are described in [Grading inputs and changes](grading.md).

## Ungraded responses

A verifier or judge request can fail for reasons unrelated to the response: a
code-service outage, a judge transport error, an unparseable verdict. That
response has no grade. Scoring it zero would place a correct answer below its
siblings' baseline and push the policy away from it; dropping its prompt group
would waste every graded sibling. By default (`core.exclude_ungraded = true`) the
compiler installs
`custom_reward_post_process_path = "open_instruct.miles.rewards.exclusion.exclude_ungraded"`:
the ungraded response gets zero advantage and a zeroed loss mask, its group's
baseline uses only the graded responses, and the paired group filter ignores it
when checking reward variation (groups with fewer than two graded responses are
dropped). The failed response keeps `metadata.reward_omission` with the verifier
name and error, and W&B reports `rollout/verification/ungraded_samples` and
`ungraded_fraction` per collection. With response-averaged loss, excluded responses
still count in the batch denominator, so a high failure fraction reduces the
policy-gradient signal per step. Groups with no trainable responses are
always rejected, even with `filter_zero_std_groups=false`; that setting keeps
valid all-zero grades, not empty groups. The collector requests replacement groups.
A run where every group is rejected makes no optimizer progress.

Set `core.exclude_ungraded = false` to return to omitting the whole prompt group
(`rollout/verification/omitted_records`). The compiler also leaves the hook out
under `core.expert_balanced_packing`, which supports no reward post-process, and
under `miles.partial_rollout`, since the hook supports single-segment rollouts
only. Custom multi-segment generators must explicitly opt out as well. A custom
`miles.custom_convert_samples_to_train_data_path` bypasses reward postprocessing:
it retains group omission, and explicitly combining it with a managed exclusion
hook is rejected. Math verifier timeouts and code-service rejections (4xx, or a 500 that
persists through its retries) are not ungraded: they keep their zero reward, as
documented under [reward-service failure policies](data-and-evaluation.md#reward-service-failure-policies).

For an explicitly documented overlong-filtering experiment that excludes truncated
responses from training instead, override the baseline with:

```toml
[core]
reward_zero_truncated = false

[miles]
custom_reward_post_process_path = "open_instruct.miles.rewards.truncation.exclude_truncated"
```

Truncated responses then get zero advantage and a zeroed loss mask, and each group's
baseline uses only its finished, graded responses (this hook also excludes
ungraded responses). Raw reward metrics are unchanged. With response-averaged
loss, excluded responses still count in the batch denominator. When zero-variance
group filtering is enabled, it also considers only finished, graded responses:
groups with fewer than two of them or no variation in their rewards are dropped
before occupying training batch slots.

## Final-answer-only rewards

Set `core.reward_final_answer_only=true` to grade only text after the last literal
`</think>` by default. A missing closing marker, whitespace-only final answer or
reopened thinking receives each response-required verifier's floor without calling
it. Set `core.reward_reasoning_mode="none"` for an explicitly non-thinking run.
This applies to text/code verifiers and named judges; named judges receive the
selected region intact, including answer tags and surrounding prose.
The full response and its token IDs remain available for training and recording.

The shared `ResponseParts` object separates thinking and the delivered answer or
action. Trusted factory/registry declarations identify answer, process, format or
composite objectives. Answer objectives use `response`; explicit process/format
objectives may select `thinking` or `full` and separately permit a missing
delivered response. ToolRL declares full context for boundary format and the
presented response for action correctness; token-length graders retain full
trajectory tokens. See the [configuration, interface and
per-path behavior register](grading.md) before changing a run's grading policy.

Verifiers can optionally implement
`async_call_final_answer(tokens, prediction, label, **kwargs)`. In final-answer
mode with a response view, the adapter uses this method when present; otherwise
it calls `async_call` with the selected string. Migrated consumers receive
`selected_input=True`, bypass their thinking-boundary logic and retain their
task-specific answer parsing. All calls run after the component's eligibility
and truncation gates. Response/thinking views receive empty token lists; full
views retain actual trajectory tokens. A structured consumer can use
`async_call_parts`; composites additionally receive separately selected component
strings. Ordinary flag-off calls retain the historical `async_call` path,
including any native thinking removal. Named judges use their sample-aware path.

The built-in `R1FormatVerifier` implements this interface: after the outer gate
selects the final section, it checks for optional leading whitespace followed by
`<answer>...</answer>`, without requiring another closing-think marker. Its
raw-response check is unchanged. This remains a format reward, not an answer
correctness or content check; it retains the existing allowance for empty answer
tags and trailing text. In final-only mode, only the last closing marker's suffix
is checked, so answer tags in an earlier section cannot earn format reward.

For native IF grading, use the built-in adapter. A complete reward registry is:

```json
{
  "ifeval": {
    "factory": "open_instruct.miles.rewards.task_verifiers.ManifestIFVerifier"
  }
}
```

The native adapter uses `IFEvalVerifier`, including its existing task
normalization in both modes. Selected-input mode bypasses its thinking split
while retaining removal of answer tags, `<|assistant|>` and outer whitespace
before grading IF constraints. R1 format
reward checks the tags themselves; IF reward grades the normalized answer.

The library option defaults to false; the maintained examples explicitly enable it
with the Olmo thinking convention. It permits
multiple closing markers, so it is not an exactly-one-tag format validator.

## Runtime images

Build an application image from the source revision you intend to run, using the
[locked runtime](architecture.md#runtime-sources-and-images). Reusing an image
runs its original code; local Python edits are not submitted with the TOML.
Use the [validation procedure](architecture.md#local-development) for source
changes, then try the selected model and topology on a small run.

## Publication modes

| Mode | Behavior and use |
|---|---|
| `core.publication_mode="refresh"` | Node and three-node templates. Preserve generated tokens and their original behavior log probabilities across publication; rebuild serving state under the new weights and continue decoding. A response can span multiple policy versions. |
| `barrier` | Low-level default, used by dev mechanics example. Does not continue mixed-policy responses across publication. |
| `engine_drain` | Independent engine drain: finish requests on their admitted version before swapping weights. This mode is distinct from mixed-policy refresh; see [engine drain](engine-drain.md). |

The [generated recipe tables](configuration.md#example-recipes) show each
starter's allocation, batch geometry, publication mode and lag limit. Read
[refresh requirements](async-pipeline.md#mixed-policy-refresh) and
[policy lag and TIS](async-pipeline.md#policy-lag-and-tis) before changing the
async recipe.

## Documentation and agent entry point

Agents discover this workflow through AGENTS.md; no
special prompt is needed. Follow the [documentation index](index.md) for model
support, configuration, data, parallelism and operations.

1	"""Expose the MILES workflow and inference-record tools through one command-line entry
2	point. The CLI loads run files and overrides for planning, validation, local
3	execution, Beaker submission and status queries, or dispatches record analysis and
4	prompt-selection commands. Runtime imports are deferred to the commands that need
5	them so planning remains available without the GPU stack.
6	
7	Run with python -m open_instruct.miles {plan,validate,train,run,status} CONFIG.toml.
8	
9	Inference-record tools use their own arguments:
10	python -m open_instruct.miles records summarize STORE --output DIR
11	python -m open_instruct.miles records select STORE --skip all_zero --output TABLE.json
12	"""
13	
14	import argparse
15	import importlib
16	import json
17	import sys
18	from pathlib import Path
19	
20	from open_instruct.miles.configuration import advisories, specs, validation
21	from open_instruct.miles.configuration.config import RunConfig
22	from open_instruct.miles.distillation import opd_config
23	from open_instruct.miles.errors import InputError
24	
25	
26	def main() -> None:
27	    if sys.argv[1:2] == ["records"]:
28	        module = (
29	            "open_instruct.miles.datasets.replay_summary"
30	            if sys.argv[2:3] == ["replay-pool"]
31	            else "open_instruct.miles.datasets.record_selection"
32	            if sys.argv[2:3] == ["select"]
33	            else "miles.utils.record_summary"
34	        )
35	        try:
36	            command = importlib.import_module(module)
37	        except ModuleNotFoundError as error:
38	            if error.name == "miles":
39	                raise SystemExit(
40	                    "Record analysis requires the MILES package; run it in the pinned runtime."
41	                ) from error
42	            raise
43	        command.main(sys.argv[3:] if sys.argv[2:3] in (["select"], ["replay-pool"]) else sys.argv[2:])
44	        return
45	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
46	    parser.add_argument("command", choices=("plan", "validate", "train", "run", "status"))
47	    parser.add_argument("config", type=Path)
48	    parser.add_argument(
49	        "--set",
50	        dest="overrides",
51	        action="append",
52	        default=[],
53	        metavar="SECTION.KEY=VALUE",
54	        help="Override a setting with a TOML value; repeatable, quote strings",
55	    )
56	    parser.add_argument("--debug", action="store_true", help="Show a full traceback for input errors")
57	    options = parser.parse_args()
58	    try:
59	        execute(parser, options)
60	    except InputError as error:
61	        if options.debug:
62	            raise
63	        parser.error(f"{options.config}: {error}")
64	
65	
66	def execute(parser, options):
67	    payload = validation.read_document(options.config)
68	    structured = "schema_version" in payload or "model" in payload
69	    config = (
70	        specs.from_dict(payload, config_path=options.config, overrides=options.overrides)
71	        if structured
72	        else RunConfig.from_dict(payload, options.overrides)
73	    )
74	    if options.command == "plan":
75	        planned = config.plan()
76	        advisories.emit(planned)
77	        print(json.dumps(planned, indent=2))
78	        return
79	    if options.command in ("run", "status"):
80	        if not structured:
81	            parser.error("run/status require a schema_version=1 run file; raw configs support plan/validate/train")
82	        launch = importlib.import_module("open_instruct.miles.execution.launch")
83	        if options.command == "run":
84	            launch.run(options.config, options.overrides)
85	        else:
86	            print(json.dumps(launch.status(config), indent=2))
87	        return
88	    if isinstance(config, opd_config.OPDRunSpec):
89	        if options.command == "validate":
90	            config.plan()
91	            print("OPD schema and allocation validated; runtime/model checks run in the candidate image")
92	        else:
93	            runtime = importlib.import_module("open_instruct.miles.distillation.opd_runtime")
94	            runtime.execute(config)
95	        return
96	    workflow = importlib.import_module("open_instruct.miles.execution.workflow")
97	    if options.command == "validate":
98	        if structured:
99	            planned_spec = config.plan()  # Validate physical allocation as well as trainer options.
100	            advisories.emit(planned_spec)
101	            print("Run schema, topology and MILES/Core options validated; inputs and runtime checked during train")
102	        else:
103	            workflow.parse_runtime(config)
104	            print("MILES arguments validated for OLMo-core")
105	        return
106	    if structured:
107	        workflow.execute(config)
108	    else:
109	        workflow.train_config(config)
110	
111	
112	if __name__ == "__main__":
113	    main()
114
